question: Which age group of children was considered to find the child sex ratio in Census 2011?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0 to 6 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Census 2011 considered children in the age group of **0 to 6 years** to calculate the child sex ratio.
 
• The child sex ratio is defined as the number of females per 1000 males in the age group of **0 to 6 years**.
 
• This age group is crucial as it indicates the **gender bias** prevalent in society at a very early age.
 
• The child sex ratio helps in understanding the **demographic trends** and the effectiveness of government policies aimed at addressing gender discrimination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Sex Ratio (CSR)**

 
 
• The child sex ratio (CSR) is a demographic measure used to compare the number of female children to male children in a population.
 
• A CSR of less than 1,000 indicates that there are fewer female children compared to male children, which often reflects social issues like female foeticide and gender discrimination.
 
• The CSR is an important indicator of gender equality in the early stages of life.
 
• Efforts to improve CSR include government policies such as Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, aimed at promoting the welfare of girl children.
 
 
 
• **Census**
 
 
• A census is an official enumeration of the population, typically recording various details of individuals.
 
• In India, the census is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The data collected through the census provides valuable insights for planning and policy-making at various levels of government.
 
• The Census 2011 is the 15th National Census of India since 1872.
 
 
 
• **Gender Ratio**
 
 
• The gender ratio refers to the ratio of males to females in a population.
 
• In many parts of the world, particularly in South Asia, gender ratios can be imbalanced due to cultural and societal factors.
 
• Efforts to balance gender ratios often involve addressing deep-seated gender biases and promoting gender equality through education, legal reforms, and social policies.
 
• A balanced gender ratio is crucial for achieving sustainable development and social stability.
